# os

Types from the Go package `os` (a library PocketBase builds on), as JavaScript sees them: they turn up as values of [PocketBase's types](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase) and of hook events.

## os.readdirMode

Has everything <code>Number</code> has.

## os.File

Has everything <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfile">file</a></code> has.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `readdir()` | <code>(n: number): Array&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfileinfo">FileInfo</a>&gt;</code> | Readdir reads the contents of the directory associated with file and returns a slice of up to n [`FileInfo`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfileinfo) values, as would be returned by `Lstat`, in directory order. Subsequent calls on the same file will yield further FileInfos. |
| `readdirnames()` | <code>(n: number): Array&lt;string&gt;</code> | Readdirnames reads the contents of the directory associated with file and returns a slice of up to n names of files in the directory, in directory order. Subsequent calls on the same file will yield further names. |
| `readDir()` | <code>(n: number): Array&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osdirentry">DirEntry</a>&gt;</code> | ReadDir reads the contents of the directory associated with the file f and returns a slice of [`DirEntry`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osdirentry) values in directory order. Subsequent calls on the same file will yield later DirEntry records in the directory. |
| `name()` | <code>(): string</code> | Name returns the name of the file as presented to Open. |
| `read()` | <code>(b: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;): number</code> | Read reads up to len(b) bytes from the File and stores them in b. It returns the number of bytes read and any error encountered. At end of file, Read returns 0, io.EOF. |
| `readAt()` | <code>(b: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;, off: number): number</code> | ReadAt reads len(b) bytes from the File starting at byte offset off. It returns the number of bytes read and the error, if any. ReadAt always returns a non-nil error when n < len(b). At end of file, that error is io.EOF. |
| `readFrom()` | <code>(r: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#ioreader">io.Reader</a>): number</code> | ReadFrom implements io.ReaderFrom. |
| `write()` | <code>(b: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;): number</code> | Write writes len(b) bytes from b to the File. It returns the number of bytes written and an error, if any. Write returns a non-nil error when n != len(b). |
| `writeAt()` | <code>(b: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;, off: number): number</code> | WriteAt writes len(b) bytes to the File starting at byte offset off. It returns the number of bytes written and an error, if any. WriteAt returns a non-nil error when n != len(b). |
| `writeTo()` | <code>(w: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#iowriter">io.Writer</a>): number</code> | WriteTo implements io.WriterTo. |
| `seek()` | <code>(offset: number, whence: number): number</code> | Seek sets the offset for the next Read or Write on file to offset, interpreted according to whence: 0 means relative to the origin of the file, 1 means relative to the current offset, and 2 means relative to the end. It returns the new offset and an error, if any. The behavior of Seek on a file opened with `O_APPEND` is not specified. |
| `writeString()` | <code>(s: string): number</code> | WriteString is like Write, but writes the contents of string s rather than a slice of bytes. |
| `chmod()` | <code>(mode: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfilemode">FileMode</a>): void</code> | Chmod changes the mode of the file to mode. If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError]. |
| `setDeadline()` | <code>(t: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime">time.Time</a>): void</code> | SetDeadline sets the read and write deadlines for a File. It is equivalent to calling both SetReadDeadline and SetWriteDeadline. |
| `setReadDeadline()` | <code>(t: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime">time.Time</a>): void</code> | SetReadDeadline sets the deadline for future Read calls and any currently-blocked Read call. A zero value for t means Read will not time out. Not all files support setting deadlines; see SetDeadline. |
| `setWriteDeadline()` | <code>(t: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timetime">time.Time</a>): void</code> | SetWriteDeadline sets the deadline for any future Write calls and any currently-blocked Write call. Even if Write times out, it may return n > 0, indicating that some of the data was successfully written. A zero value for t means Write will not time out. Not all files support setting deadlines; see SetDeadline. |
| `syscallConn()` | <code>(): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/syscall#syscallrawconn">syscall.RawConn</a></code> | SyscallConn returns a raw file. This implements the syscall.Conn interface. |
| `fd()` | <code>(): number</code> | Fd returns the system file descriptor or handle referencing the open file. If f is closed, the descriptor becomes invalid. If f is garbage collected, a finalizer may close the descriptor, making it invalid; see `runtime.setFinalizer` for more information on when a finalizer might be run. |
| `close()` | <code>(): void</code> | Close closes the [`File`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfile), rendering it unusable for I/O. On files that support [`File.setDeadline`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfile), any pending I/O operations will be canceled and return immediately with an `ErrClosed` error. Close will return an error if it has already been called. |
| `chown()` | <code>(uid: number, gid: number): void</code> | Chown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file. If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError]. |
| `truncate()` | <code>(size: number): void</code> | Truncate changes the size of the file. It does not change the I/O offset. If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError]. |
| `sync()` | <code>(): void</code> | Sync commits the current contents of the file to stable storage. Typically, this means flushing the file system's in-memory copy of recently written data to disk. |
| `chdir()` | <code>(): void</code> | Chdir changes the current working directory to the file, which must be a directory. If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError]. |
| `stat()` | <code>(): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfileinfo">FileInfo</a></code> | Stat returns the [`FileInfo`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfileinfo) structure describing file. If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError]. |

## os.Process

Process stores the information about a process created by `StartProcess`.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `pid` | <code>number</code> | Pid is the operating system process ID. |
| `release()` | <code>(): void</code> | Release releases any resources associated with the [`Process`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osprocess) p, rendering it unusable in the future. Release only needs to be called if [`Process.wait`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osprocess) is not. |
| `kill()` | <code>(): void</code> | Kill causes the [`Process`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osprocess) to exit immediately. Kill does not wait until the Process has actually exited. This only kills the Process itself, not any other processes it may have started. |
| `wait()` | <code>(): (<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osprocessstate">ProcessState</a>)</code> | Wait waits for the [`Process`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osprocess) to exit, and then returns a ProcessState describing its status and an error, if any. Wait releases any resources associated with the Process. On most operating systems, the Process must be a child of the current process or an error will be returned. |
| `signal()` | <code>(sig: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#ossignal">Signal</a>): void</code> | Signal sends a signal to the [`Process`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osprocess). Sending `Interrupt` on Windows is not implemented. |
| `withHandle()` | <code>(f: (handle: number) =&gt; void): void</code> | WithHandle calls a supplied function f with a valid process handle as an argument. The handle is guaranteed to refer to process p until f returns, even if p terminates. This function cannot be used after [`Process.release`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osprocess) or [`Process.wait`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osprocess). |

## os.processHandle

processHandle holds an operating system handle to a process.
This is only used on systems that support that concept,
currently Linux and Windows.
This maintains a reference count to the handle,
and closes the handle when the reference drops to zero.

## os.ProcAttr

ProcAttr holds the attributes that will be applied to a new process
started by StartProcess.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `dir` | <code>string</code> | If Dir is non-empty, the child changes into the directory before creating the process. |
| `env` | <code>Array&lt;string&gt;</code> | If Env is non-nil, it gives the environment variables for the new process in the form returned by Environ. If it is nil, the result of Environ will be used. |
| `files` | <code>Array&lt;(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfile">File</a> &#124; undefined)&gt;</code> | Files specifies the open files inherited by the new process. The first three entries correspond to standard input, standard output, and standard error. An implementation may support additional entries, depending on the underlying operating system. A nil entry corresponds to that file being closed when the process starts. On Unix systems, StartProcess will change these File values to blocking mode, which means that SetDeadline will stop working and calling Close will not interrupt a Read or Write. |
| `sys?` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/syscall#syscallsysprocattr">syscall.SysProcAttr</a></code> | Operating system-specific process creation attributes. Note that setting this field means that your program may not execute properly or even compile on some operating systems. |

| `success()` | <code>(): boolean</code> | Success reports whether the program exited successfully, such as with exit status 0 on Unix. |
| `sys()` | <code>(): any</code> | Sys returns system-dependent exit information about the process. Convert it to the appropriate underlying type, such as `syscall.waitStatus` on Unix, to access its contents. |
| `sysUsage()` | <code>(): any</code> | SysUsage returns system-dependent resource usage information about the exited process. Convert it to the appropriate underlying type, such as [*syscall.Rusage] on Unix, to access its contents. (On Unix, *syscall.Rusage matches struct rusage as defined in the getrusage(2) manual page.) |
| `pid()` | <code>(): number</code> | Pid returns the process id of the exited process. |
| `string()` | <code>(): string</code> |  |
| `exitCode()` | <code>(): number</code> | ExitCode returns the exit code of the exited process, or -1 if the process hasn't exited or was terminated by a signal. |

## os.Root

Root may be used to only access files within a single directory tree.

Methods on Root can only access files and directories beneath a root directory.
If any component of a file name passed to a method of Root references a location
outside the root, the method returns an error.
File names may reference the directory itself (.).

Methods on Root will follow symbolic links, but symbolic links may not
reference a location outside the root.
Symbolic links must not be absolute.

Methods on Root do not prohibit traversal of filesystem boundaries,
Linux bind mounts, /proc special files, or access to Unix device files.

Methods on Root are safe to be used from multiple goroutines simultaneously.

On most platforms, creating a Root opens a file descriptor or handle referencing
the directory. If the directory is moved, methods on Root reference the original
directory in its new location.

Root's behavior differs on some platforms:

```
  - When GOOS=windows, file names may not reference Windows reserved device names
    such as NUL and COM1.
  - On Unix, [Root.Chmod], [Root.Chown], and [Root.Chtimes] are vulnerable to a race condition.
    If the target of the operation is changed from a regular file to a symlink
    while the operation is in progress, the operation may be performed on the link
    rather than the link target.
  - When GOOS=js, Root is vulnerable to TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use)
    attacks in symlink validation, and cannot ensure that operations will not
    escape the root.
  - When GOOS=plan9 or GOOS=js, Root does not track directories across renames.
    On these platforms, a Root references a directory name, not a file descriptor.
  - WASI preview 1 (GOOS=wasip1) does not support [Root.Chmod].
```

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|

## os.sysfdType

sysfdType is the native type of a file handle
(int on Unix, syscall.Handle on Windows),
permitting helper functions to be written portably.

Has everything <code>Number</code> has.

## os.FileInfo

A FileInfo describes a file and is returned by `Stat` and `Lstat`.

Has everything <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/fs#fsfileinfo">fs.FileInfo</a></code> has.

## os.FileMode

A FileMode represents a file's mode and permission bits.
The bits have the same definition on all systems, so that
information about files can be moved from one system
to another portably. Not all bits apply to all systems.
The only required bit is `ModeDir` for directories.

Has everything <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/fs#fsfilemode">fs.FileMode</a></code> has.
